artifact: Denying Knowledge v0.10 PC2 claim and evidence ledger

claims.claim: The description and commitment registers are distinguished primarily by principal speech-act function and assessment standard rather than by two exhaustive semantic species.
claims.scope_or_condition: Stable content may occur in both registers; mixed and practice-bound cases require decomposition.

claims.claim: Descriptive uses remain answerable to evidence, truth, valid inference, calibration, and proof relative to declared assumptions.
claims.scope_or_condition: Religious, moral, or metaphysical subject matter does not exempt descriptive work from descriptive standards.

claims.claim: Commitment uses are assessed through warrant, integrity, protected viability, affected-party standing, consequence, correction, and repair.
claims.scope_or_condition: No single scalar or theorem supplies all practical content.

claims.claim: Mixed utterances should be decomposed so that descriptive, commitment, symbolic, and normative components answer to their appropriate standards.
claims.scope_or_condition: Decomposition is interpretive and may remain contested.

claims.claim: Established descriptive facts constrain commitment, while commitment warrant does not establish descriptive fact.
claims.scope_or_condition: Commitments may motivate inquiry but do not count as evidence for the hypotheses they inspire.

claims.claim: Adopting the two-register discipline is itself a defeasible commitment grounded in a broader commitment to truth.
claims.scope_or_condition: The framework must remain revisable by its own standards.

claims.claim: The formal architecture assumes a Boolean-closed representable commitment fragment with stable realization conditions.
claims.scope_or_condition: Ritual, prayer, myth, poetry, and other practice-bound contents may fall outside this formalization.

claims.claim: Descriptive truth-satisfaction and commitment realization should be notationally distinguished as ⊨_D and ⊩_R.
claims.scope_or_condition: The distinction marks different interpretive roles, not necessarily disjoint ontological content types.

claims.claim: Within one model, premises filter a fixed viability base by intersection.
claims.scope_or_condition: Changing floors, affected scope, horizon, ordering, option set, or realization semantics is model revision.

claims.claim: Smooth fixed-base preferential models over the declared Boolean fragment satisfy System P on the relevant definability domain.
claims.scope_or_condition: Requires stable realization conditions, Boolean closure, definability, and smoothness.

claims.claim: Ranked models support Rational Monotony when every relevant nonempty definable set attains a minimum.
claims.scope_or_condition: Total rank order alone is insufficient without minimum attainment.

claims.claim: The System P Or rule is claimed only where disjunction is defined and realization extensions satisfy the Boolean union clause.
claims.scope_or_condition: No full Or claim is made for unformalized sets of practices or commitments.

claims.claim: Strong warrant holds when every nonempty best viable realization supports the commitment.
claims.scope_or_condition: This is skeptical preferential consequence relative to the declared model.

claims.claim: Admissibility holds when at least one nonempty best viable realization supports the commitment.
claims.scope_or_condition: Admissibility includes strong warrant.

claims.claim: Mere admissibility is the strict middle case in which at least one but not every best realization supports the commitment.
claims.scope_or_condition: Requires a non-singleton best set with divided support.

claims.claim: Credulous admissibility can fail conjunction and is not itself a System P consequence relation.
claims.scope_or_condition: Two tied best worlds separately support φ and ψ while neither supports their conjunction.

claims.claim: Exclusion holds when no nonempty best viable realization supports the commitment.
claims.scope_or_condition: Relative to the declared model; not physical impossibility.

claims.claim: Within the adopted classical Boolean fragment, exclusion of φ is extensionally equivalent to strong warrant for ¬φ.
claims.scope_or_condition: The convention may flatten the practical difference between absence of support and positive commitment to cessation.

claims.claim: Infeasibility means that no premise-compatible viable realization exists.
claims.scope_or_condition: Infeasibility is distinct from underdetermination and is not permission by default.

claims.claim: Underdetermination means that compatible possibilities remain but the model cannot responsibly discriminate.
claims.scope_or_condition: May arise from non-attainment, incomplete ordering, unsettled facts, omitted parties or options, or model uncertainty.

claims.claim: The inherited maximum-preservation clause can hold only as equality after restriction and is equivalent, when maxima are attained, to support by at least one old maximizer.
claims.scope_or_condition: It captures credulous admissibility, not skeptical consequence.

claims.claim: Transformative commitments can be represented through trajectories inside a fixed model.
claims.scope_or_condition: Trajectory-level viability and ordering must remain fixed for the System P result to apply.

claims.claim: A change to floors, affected scope, horizon, ordering, option set, or realization semantics is a model revision and cannot silently inherit the prior verdict.
claims.scope_or_condition: A bridge argument must identify what has been preserved and changed.

claims.claim: Practical expansion warrant is not supplied by KLM form alone.
claims.scope_or_condition: Requires substantive factual, ethical, social, and institutional content.

claims.claim: Public specification makes model capture visible but does not make a model contestable.
claims.scope_or_condition: Contestability requires standing, option-set integrity, independent challenge, correctability, and noncompensation.

claims.claim: The formal verdict relation is model-relative rather than intersubjectively objective without qualification.
claims.scope_or_condition: Reproducibility within shared premises does not justify the premises themselves.

claims.claim: Transparent cross-model disagreement may be a legitimate endpoint when no justified bridge selects among adequate competing models.
claims.scope_or_condition: The framework can require disclosure and comparison without promising forced convergence.

claims.claim: KLM preferential consequence presupposes stable realization conditions and is orthogonal to the compositional question posed by Frege–Geach.
claims.scope_or_condition: KLM governs consequence over interpreted contents; it does not create their meaning.

claims.claim: For already-representable contents with stable realization conditions, fixed-base preferential semantics supplies a defeasible consequence structure through embedded inference.
claims.scope_or_condition: This is a consequence claim, not a general semantics of ritual, prayer, poetry, myth, or contemplative avowal.

claims.claim: The paper does not claim novelty for Boolean practical semantics, plan or imperative semantics, formal expressivism, KLM logic, or two-register religious analysis.
claims.scope_or_condition: Relevant prior work includes Gibbard, Yalcin, Charlow, and the Wittgensteinian debate.

claims.claim: The paper’s distinctive proposal is the combination of stable commitment contents with fixed-base nonmonotonic consequence and a practical taxonomy separating every-best from some-best support.
claims.scope_or_condition: Novelty remains subject to specialist literature review.

claims.claim: The two-widows case is schematic, stipulated, non-clinical, and cannot diagnose suppression from behavior alone.
claims.scope_or_condition: Quiet, delayed, nonexpressive, or culturally unfamiliar grief may be healthy.

claims.claim: Deferred inquiry requires preserved anomaly, expiry, capacity-building, independent support, protected exit, attention to affected others, and review outside the benefiting community.
claims.scope_or_condition: Deferral is not a license for indefinite institutional control of inquiry.

claims.claim: Symmetry of evidential method does not imply symmetry of evidence or factual verdict.
claims.scope_or_condition: Equal standards properly produce unequal conclusions when evidence differs.

claims.claim: Compassion changes the responsible response to a person without changing the truth value of their claim or creating an educational duty for those harmed.
claims.scope_or_condition: Compassion does not erase accountability, boundaries, or repair.

claims.claim: The two-register discipline commits the framework to revision in both registers and to making reality more important than identity built around interpretation.
claims.scope_or_condition: Descriptive revision follows evidence; commitment revision follows fact, trajectory, standing, consequence, and correction.

claims.claim: Finite three-world regression protects implementation of System P, Rational Monotony, fixed-base filtering, maximum-preservation equivalence, and practical-verdict guards.
claims.scope_or_condition: Finite enumeration is not a representation theorem or philosophical validation.

claims.claim: In the complete finite regression, all 4,104 no-best-set cases are infeasible rather than underdetermined, because every nonempty finite strict partial order has a minimal element.
claims.scope_or_condition: Underdetermination is tested separately as a model-adequacy condition.

claims.claim: A targeted non-singleton-best stratum contains 73 model configurations, 584 commitment cases, and all 294 mere-admissibility cases in the finite suite.
claims.scope_or_condition: This protects the implementation of the middle verdict but does not establish its empirical frequency.
